The EST I Mathematics section tests core algebraic reasoning, problem-solving, and quantitative analysis in two parts — one without a calculator and one with. It is the primary university-admissions standardised test for international and American-diploma students across the Middle East.

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST I — Literacy & Math), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

label.en: ⏱ EST I Math Section Pacing & Calculator Strategy
label.ar: ⏱ EST I Math Section Pacing & Calculator Strategy (نظام اختبار EST I واستراتيجيات الحل)

body.en:
• Section I (No-Calculator): 20 questions in 25 minutes = 75 seconds per question. Prioritize quick mental factoring, linear equation isolation, and slope formulas. Bank easy questions in under 45 seconds to leave buffer time for the final grid-in items.
  • Section II (Calculator Permitted): 38 questions in 55 minutes = ~87 seconds per question. Use your calculator strategically to verify quadratic solutions, percentage chains, and complex statistical summaries. Never waste time typing arithmetic you can compute mentally.
  • Zero Guessing Penalty: Since there is no negative marking, never leave any question blank. With 60 seconds left, fill in answers for all remaining blank items.

label.en: ▲ The 4 Core Commandments for Scoring 750+ on EST I Math
label.ar: ▲ The 4 Core Commandments for Scoring 750+ on EST I Math (نظام اختبار EST I واستراتيجيات الحل)

body.en:
• 1. Linear Systems by Ratio Inspection: For the system \(a_1x + b_1y = c_1\) and \(a_2x + b_2y = c_2\): if \(\frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \frac{c_1}{c_2}\), the lines are parallel (no solution). If all three ratios are equal, they are coincident (infinitely many solutions).
  • 2. Quadratic Discriminant Check: Before applying the full quadratic formula or attempting complex factoring, compute \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\). If \(\Delta < 0\), there are no real roots; if \(\Delta = 0\), one repeated rational root; if \(\Delta > 0\) and a perfect square, rational roots exist.
  • 3. Percentage Change Denominator Rule: Percentage change is always calculated as \(\frac{\text{new} - \text{old}}{\text{old}} \times 100\%\). Never divide by the new value! A 25% increase followed by a 20% decrease returns to the original value: \(1.25 \times 0.80 = 1.00\).
  • 4. Angle Mode & Circle Geometry: Verify whether angles are in radians or degrees. Remember that arc length \(s = r\theta\) (where \(\theta\) is in radians) and sector area \(A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta\). In degrees, \(s = \frac{\theta}{360} 2\pi r\) and \(A = \frac{\theta}{360} \pi r^2\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Test format & strategy)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Test format & strategy)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example A — Test format & strategy (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول A — Test format & strategy (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): The graph of the function \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \) is shown below. The vertex of the parabola is at the point \( (-2, 5) \) and the parabola passes through the point \( (0, 9) \). What is the value of \( b \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: The vertex form of a quadratic function is given by \( f(x) = a(x-h)^2 + k \), where \( (h, k) \) is the vertex. In this case, the vertex is \( (-2, 5) \), so \( h = -2 \) and \( k = 5 \). Thus, the function can be written as \( f(x) = a(x - (-2))^2 + 5 \), which simplifies to \( f(x) = a(x+2)^2 + 5 \). The parabola also passes through the point \( (0, 9) \). We can substitute these values into the equation to solve for \( a \): \[ 9 = a(0+2)^2 + 5 \] \[ 9 = a(2)^2 + 5 \] \[ 9 = 4a + 5 \] \[ 4 = 4a \] \[ a = 1 \] Now we have the function in vertex form: \( f(x) = (x+2)^2 + 5 \). To find the value of \( b \), we expand this expression to the standard form \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \): \[ f(x) = (x^2 + 4x + 4) + 5 \] \[ f(x) = x^2 + 4x + 9 \] Comparing this to \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \), we have \( a = 1 \), \( b = 4 \), and \( c = 9 \). The question asks for the value of \( b \).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): The التمثيل البياني of the الدالة \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \) is shown below. The الرأس of the القطع المكافئ is at the point \( (-2, 5) \) and the القطع المكافئ passes through the point \( (0, 9) \). What is the value of \( b \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: The الرأس form of a quadratic الدالة is المعطيات by \( f(x) = a(x-h)^2 + k \), حيث \( (h, k) \) is the الرأس. In this case, the الرأس is \( (-2, 5) \), so \( h = -2 \) and \( k = 5 \). وعليه, the الدالة can be written as \( f(x) = a(x - (-2))^2 + 5 \), which simplifies to \( f(x) = a(x+2)^2 + 5 \). The القطع المكافئ also passes through the point \( (0, 9) \). We can عوّض these values into the المعادلة to أوجد قيمة \( a \): \[ 9 = a(0+2)^2 + 5 \] \[ 9 = a(2)^2 + 5 \] \[ 9 = 4a + 5 \] \[ 4 = 4a \] \[ a = 1 \] Now we have the الدالة in الرأس form: \( f(x) = (x+2)^2 + 5 \). To أوجد قيمة \( b \), we expand this العبارة الجبرية to the standard form \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \): \[ f(x) = (x^2 + 4x + 4) + 5 \] \[ f(x) = x^2 + 4x + 9 \] Comparing this to \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \), we have \( a = 1 \), \( b = 4 \), and \( c = 9 \). The question asks for the value of \( b \).

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — Test format & strategy (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(B\) — Test format & strategy (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): The diagram shows a triangle ABC, where D is a point on side AB and E is a point on side AC. It is given that DE is parallel to BC. If AD = 6 cm, DB = 4 cm, AE = 9 cm, and DE = 12 cm, find the length of the side BC.

Step-by-Step Solution: Since DE is parallel to BC, triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC by the AA similarity criterion (angle A is common, and \( \angle ADE = \angle ABC \) and \( \angle AED = \angle ACB \) as corresponding angles). For similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides is equal. Therefore, we have: \[ \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{AE}{AC} = \frac{DE}{BC} \] We know AD = 6 cm and DB = 4 cm, so AB = AD + DB = 6 + 4 = 10 cm. We are given AE = 9 cm and DE = 12 cm. Let BC = x cm. Using the ratio of corresponding sides: \[ \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC} \] \[ \frac{6}{10} = \frac{12}{x} \] To solve for x, we can cross-multiply: \[ 6x = 10 \times 12 \] \[ 6x = 120 \] \[ x = \frac{120}{6} \] \[ x = 20 \] Therefore, the length of the side BC is 20 cm.
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): The المخطط shows a المثلث ABC, حيث D is a point on side AB and E is a point on side AC. It is بما أن DE is parallel to BC. If AD = 6 cm, DB = 4 cm, AE = 9 cm, and DE = 12 cm, أوجد length of the side BC.

Step-by-Step الحل: Since DE is parallel to BC, المثلث ADE is similar to المثلث ABC by the AA similarity criterion (الزاوية A is common, and \( \angle ADE = \angle ABC \) and \( \angle AED = \angle ACB \) as corresponding angles). For similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides is equal. وبالتالي, we have: \[ \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{AE}{AC} = \frac{DE}{BC} \] We know AD = 6 cm and DB = 4 cm, so AB = AD + DB = 6 + 4 = 10 cm. We are المعطيات AE = 9 cm and DE = 12 cm. Let BC = x cm. Using the ratio of corresponding sides: \[ \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC} \] \[ \frac{6}{10} = \frac{12}{x} \] To أوجد قيمة x, we can cross-multiply: \[ 6x = 10 \times 12 \] \[ 6x = 120 \] \[ x = \frac{120}{6} \] \[ x = 20 \] وبالتالي, the length of the side BC is 20 cm.

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — Test format & strategy (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(C\) — Test format & strategy (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Consider the functions \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \) and \( g(x) = x + 7 \). At what \( x \)-value do the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect?

Step-by-Step Solution: To find the x-value where the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect, we set the two functions equal to each other: \( f(x) = g(x) \). Substituting the given expressions for \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \): \( 2x + 3 = x + 7 \) To solve for \( x \), subtract \( x \) from both sides of the equation: \( 2x - x + 3 = x - x + 7 \) This simplifies to: \( x + 3 = 7 \) Next, subtract 3 from both sides of the equation: \( x + 3 - 3 = 7 - 3 \) Which gives the solution: \( x = 4 \) Therefore, the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect at \( x = 4 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): Consider the الدوال \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \) and \( g(x) = x + 7 \). At what \( x \)-value do the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect?

Step-by-Step الحل: To أوجد x-value حيث the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect, we set the two الدوال equal to each other: \( f(x) = g(x) \). Substituting the المعطيات expressions for \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \): \( 2x + 3 = x + 7 \) To أوجد قيمة \( x \), subtract \( x \) from both sides of the المعادلة: \( 2x - x + 3 = x - x + 7 \) This simplifies to: \( x + 3 = 7 \) Next, subtract 3 from both sides of the المعادلة: \( x + 3 - 3 = 7 - 3 \) Which gives the الحل: \( x = 4 \) Therefore, the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect at \( x = 4 \).

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Test format & strategy (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — Test format & strategy (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): A recipe calls for \( 2 \) cups of flour for every \( 3 \) cups of sugar. If \( 8 \) cups of flour are used, how many cups of sugar are needed?

Step-by-Step Solution: Let \( F \) be the amount of flour and \( S \) be the amount of sugar. The ratio of flour to sugar is given as \( \frac{F}{S} = \frac{2}{3} \). We are given that \( F = 8 \) cups. We need to find \( S \). We can set up the proportion: \( \frac{8}{S} = \frac{2}{3} \). To solve for \( S \), we can cross-multiply: \( 8 \times 3 = 2 \times S \). This simplifies to \( 24 = 2S \). Dividing both sides by 2, we get \( S = \frac{24}{2} = 12 \). Therefore, 12 cups of sugar are needed.

question.en: Section I of EST I Math contains 20 questions in 25 minutes. If a student answers the first 12 questions in an average of 50 seconds each, how many seconds per question are available for the remaining 8 questions?
question.ar: Section I of EST I Math contains 20 questions in 25 minutes. إذا كان a student answers the first 12 questions in an average of 50 seconds each, how many seconds per question are available for the remaining 8 questions?

solution.en: \(\text{Time for first 12 questions} = 12 \times 50 = 600\text{ seconds}\) (10 minutes). \(\text{Total time} = 25 \times 60 = 1500\text{ seconds}\). \(\text{Remaining time} = 1500 - 600 = 900\text{ seconds}\). For the remaining 8 questions: \(\frac{900}{8} = 112.5\text{ seconds per question}\) (1 minute 52.5 seconds per question).

question.en: [Practice 2 · Easy] If \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), what is the value of \( x \)?
question.ar: [Practice 2 · Easy] إذا كان \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), ما قيمة \( x \)?

hints.en: To solve the equation \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), express both sides in terms of a common base: 1. Recognize that both \( 9 \) and \( 27 \) are powers of \( 3 \):.
hints.ar: To حل المعادلة \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), express both sides in terms of a common base: 1. Recognize that both \( 9 \) and \( 27 \) are powers of \( 3 \):.

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \(9 = 3^2 \quad \text{and} \quad 27 = 3^3\) Substitute these into the original equation: \((3^2)^{x+1} = (3^3)^{x-1}\).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \(9 = 3^2 \quad \text{and} \quad 27 = 3^3\) عوّض these into the original equation: \((3^2)^{x+1} = (3^3)^{x-1}\).

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(2 + 3 = 3x - 2x\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(2 + 3 = 3x - 2x\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
To solve the equation \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), express both sides in terms of a common base:

1. Recognize that both \( 9 \) and \( 27 \) are powers of \( 3 \):
   \[ 9 = 3^2 \quad \text{and} \quad 27 = 3^3 \]

2. Substitute these into the original equation:
   \[ (3^2)^{x+1} = (3^3)^{x-1} \]

3. Use the power of a power rule, \( (a^m)^n = a^{mn} \), distributing across both terms in each exponent:
   \[ 3^{2(x+1)} = 3^{3(x-1)} \]
   \[ 3^{2x+2} = 3^{3x-3} \]

4. Since the bases are equal and positive (and not equal to 1), equate the exponents:
   \[ 2x + 2 = 3x - 3 \]
   \[ 2 + 3 = 3x - 2x \]
   \[ x = 5 \]

Common misconceptions:
- Forgetting to distribute the factor to the constant term (e.g., writing \( 2x + 1 = 3x - 1 \)) yields \( x = 2 \).
- Treating the bases as linear multipliers (e.g., \( 9(x+1) = 27(x-1) \)) also incorrectly leads to \( x = 2 \).
solution.ar:
To حل المعادلة \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), express both sides in terms of a common base:

1. Recognize that both \( 9 \) and \( 27 \) are powers of \( 3 \):
   \[ 9 = 3^2 \quad \text{and} \quad 27 = 3^3 \]

2. عوّض these into the original equation:
   \[ (3^2)^{x+1} = (3^3)^{x-1} \]

3. Use the power of a power rule, \( (a^m)^n = a^{mn} \), distributing across both terms in each exponent:
   \[ 3^{2(x+1)} = 3^{3(x-1)} \]
   \[ 3^{2x+2} = 3^{3x-3} \]

4. Since the bases are equal and positive (and not equal to 1), equate the exponents:
   \[ 2x + 2 = 3x - 3 \]
   \[ 2 + 3 = 3x - 2x \]
   \[ x = 5 \]

Common misconceptions:
- Forgetting to distribute the حلّل to the constant term (e.g., writing \( 2x + 1 = 3x - 1 \)) yields \( x = 2 \).
- Treating the bases as linear multipliers (e.g., \( 9(x+1) = 27(x-1) \)) also incorrectly leads to \( x = 2 \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] The bar chart below shows the number of students who participated in different sports. The number of students who participated in swimming is unknown and represented by \( x \). If the total number of students who participated in all sports is 120, and the number of students who participated in basketball, volleyball, and soccer are 40, 30, and 20 respectively, what is the value of \( x \)?
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] The bar chart below shows the number of students who participated in dإذا كانferent sports. The number of students who participated in swimming is unknown and represented by \( x \). إذا كان the total number of students who participated in all sports is 120, and the number of students who participated in basketball, volleyball, and soccer are 40, 30, and 20 respectively, ما قيمة \( x \)?

hints.en: The bar chart represents the number of students in different sports. Let the number of students in swimming be \( x \).
hints.ar: The bar chart represents the number of students in dإذا كانferent sports. ليكن the number of students in swimming be \( x \).

hints.en: The number of students who participated in basketball is 40. The number of students who participated in volleyball is 30.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة The number of students who participated in basketball is 40. The number of students who participated in volleyball is 30. لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Therefore, the number of students who participated in swimming is 30.
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the number of students who participated in swimming is 30.

solution.en:
The bar chart represents the number of students in different sports. Let the number of students in swimming be \( x \).
The number of students who participated in basketball is 40.
The number of students who participated in volleyball is 30.
The number of students who participated in soccer is 20.
The total number of students who participated in all sports is 120.
To find the value of \( x \), we can set up an equation where the sum of students in each sport equals the total number of students:
\[ x + 40 + 30 + 20 = 120 \]
Combine the known numbers:
\[ x + 90 = 120 \]
Subtract 90 from both sides to solve for \( x \):
\[ x = 120 - 90 \]
\[ x = 30 \]
Therefore, the number of students who participated in swimming is 30.

question.en: [Practice 5 · Medium] The diagram shows the graphs of the exponential function \( y = a \cdot b^x \) and the linear function \( y = mx + c \). The exponential function passes through the points \( (0, 5) \) and \( (2, 45) \). The linear function passes through the points \( (0, 5) \) and \( (3, 20) \). Find the value of \( a \).
question.ar: [Practice 5 · Medium] The diagram shows the graphs of the exponential function \( y = a \cdot b^x \) and the linear function \( y = mx + c \). The exponential function يمر بالنقطة the points \( (0, 5) \) and \( (2, 45) \). The linear function يمر بالنقطة the points \( (0, 5) \) and \( (3, 20) \). أوجد قيمة \( a \).

hints.en: For the exponential function \( y = a \cdot b^x \): 1. Using the point \( (0, 5) \):.
hints.ar: For the exponential function \( y = a \cdot b^x \): 1. باستخدام point \( (0, 5) \):.

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \( 5 = a \cdot b^0 \) Since \( b^0 = 1 \) for any non-zero \( b \), we have \( 5 = a \cdot 1 \), which means \( a = 5 \).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \( 5 = a \cdot b^0 \) Since \( b^0 = 1 \) for any non-zero \( b \), we have \( 5 = a \cdot 1 \), which means \( a = 5 \).

hints.en: The question asks for the value of \(a\), which is the coefficient of the exponential term.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(a\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
For the exponential function \( y = a \cdot b^x \):

1. Using the point \( (0, 5) \):
   \( 5 = a \cdot b^0 \)
   Since \( b^0 = 1 \) for any non-zero \( b \), we have \( 5 = a \cdot 1 \), which means \( a = 5 \).

2. Using the point \( (2, 45) \) and the value of \( a = 5 \):
   \( 45 = 5 \cdot b^2 \)
   Divide by 5:
   \( 9 = b^2 \)
   Taking the positive square root (as bases of exponential functions are typically positive), \( b = 3 \).

So, the exponential function is \( y = 5 \cdot 3^x \).

For the linear function \( y = mx + c \):

1. Using the point \( (0, 5) \):
   \( 5 = m(0) + c \)
   This gives \( c = 5 \).

2. Using the point \( (3, 20) \) and \( c = 5 \):
   \( 20 = m(3) + 5 \)
   Subtract 5 from both sides:
   \( 15 = 3m \)
   Divide by 3:
   \( m = 5 \).

So, the linear function is \( y = 5x + 5 \).

The question asks for the value of \( a \), which is the coefficient of the exponential term.
